name: Turn know-how and videos into SOPs and training
summary: Turns know-how pages and walkthrough videos into SOP pages and training. A draft SOP goes into the business's wiki, is published once a person approves it, then each trainee gets an Asana task and a training email, both approved before they go. Crons read and draft; a person approves every publish, assignment and email.

covered_by.record-video: intake (video links arrive in the walkthrough email; the owner records the video)
covered_by.write-sop: skill (outline into a proposal), then draft (SOP page in draft)
covered_by.review-approve: approval (a person reads the draft page and approves the publish)
covered_by.assign-training: train (Asana task assigned and training email, both approved)
covered_by.train-new-hire: train (one task and one email per trainee per SOP)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: New know-how pages from the source space and walkthrough emails: one stored source each.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Write each source that has an SOP outline into a draft SOP page, and queue its publish for approval.

crons.name: train
crons.summary: After an SOP is published, one Asana training task and one training email per trainee, drafted and queued for approval.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: a read of the know-how pages and the walkthrough emails, an SOP page in draft, an unassigned Asana task in the training project, an Outlook draft. Publishing an SOP, assigning a task and sending an email are live operations and wait for a person.

confluence.covers: know-how pages from a source space; SOP pages created as drafts in the SOP space; publish on approval

microsoft-365.covers: walkthrough emails from a mailbox folder; training emails as Outlook drafts; sending through the approval queue

asana.covers: one unassigned training task per trainee per SOP; assignment on approval

gaps: Loom: not a platform in the kit. Walkthrough videos are reached through the link in the email, and the agent watches them; no transcript is pulled.
Claude, GPT and AI agents (named in 8 mentions, the tools most used to write SOPs): the model is the agent, not a kit platform. Writing the outline is a skill step, not an adapter.

No command writes an SOP outline into the store yet. The quoting propose command is quoting-only and core is not editable here, so the outline has to be written into the proposals namespace by the CRM shell or a later core change.
Confluence publish sends the draft's own version number. Confluence accepting that for a draft page is unverified until a sandbox SOP space proves it.
Record-keeping (staff have seen each SOP): Confluence and Asana read receipts are not mapped as used here, so completion is not read back. Asana task completion is a person's check.
Update-when-changed (a designated person centralises feedback and revises SOPs): nothing watches a published SOP for edits or for new know-how, so revisions are a person's step.
Wunderbuild and Mirror maps: not platforms in the kit. Their SOPs are written and shared by hand in this build.
Owners recording their own know-how, interviews, and the choice of which SOPs a trainee needs are people's judgment, not automated. Every trainee currently receives every published SOP.
Notion, SOP apps and other wikis have no mapped operations here.
Every adapter is docs-only until a sandbox Confluence space, Microsoft 365 developer tenant and Asana workspace prove it.
